I have been assigned a task which will primarily involve work done in the devops monorepo here, but it may also involve some work done in ardoq api. the work involves replacing existing natural language to gremlin conversion with nl to sparql. This is the query generator functionality. I would like you to map out where the relevant code that I would need to either work directly with or know about is located, as well as concisely and very clearly summarise the overall structure (as in which files, responsibilities are involved) currently define the gremlin flow. Here is the description of the ontology work, I will work as mentioned with the query generator: This page describes the system we are building to give LLM agents a formal understanding of Ardoq metamodels and customer data. It is a starting point for discussion, not a finished plan.

Initial page authored via Claude.

Overview and Background
Agents work dramatically better when they are given an ontology describing the data they are reasoning about. That observation is the motivation for everything below.

We produce a System Ontology two ways: by extracting it from an Ardoq metamodel, and by generating it from a system's written documentation.

That ontology then drives three downstream capabilities: data quality analysis, query generation, and (planned) EA modeling recommendations.

Ontology extraction and generation are done. Data quality analysis and query generation exist as working POCs. Reporting and the EA Modeling Analyzer have not started.

Longer term, ontologies flow back into Ardoq to improve metamodels. That work is deliberately paused pending the GraphLake storage migration.

Why Ontologies
Two independent reasons, both worth stating explicitly because they appeal to different audiences.

Agents need to be told what the data means. An agent handed a raw Ardoq workspace sees component types and reference types with no semantics attached. Handed an ontology, it sees classes, relationships, cardinalities, domains and ranges — and, importantly, intent. In our work so far this has proven to be a highly effective way to communicate both data structure and intent to an agent. Better grounding produces better queries, fewer hallucinated relationships, and analysis that reflects what the customer actually modelled.

Ontologies are a more capable modeling language than what Ardoq has today. Ardoq's current metamodel capabilities are deliberately simple — notably, there is no inheritance. OWL gives us subclassing, property hierarchies, disjointness, cardinality constraints, and a well-understood body of tooling and theory. As Ardoq's storage layer moves to RDF (see GraphLake), expressing EA metamodels as OWL becomes a natural fit rather than a translation exercise.

The second reason is why this work matters beyond the immediate agent use cases: the same artifact that makes agents smarter today is the artifact that makes the metamodel richer tomorrow.

The workflow at a glance
Ontology Workflows.png
Reading the diagram left to right:

Two sources feed one artifact. An existing Ardoq metamodel (top left) and a corpus of system documentation (bottom left) are each converted into ontology form and consolidated into the System Ontology.

The System Ontology is the hub. Everything downstream reads from it. It is also fed back in as context to the agents in the Data Quality Analyzer and Query Generator (the forward path along the top of the diagram), so those agents reason against the full model rather than a fragment.

Two consumers. The Data Quality Analyzer → Query Generator → Report Generator chain finds and reports problems in customer data. The EA Modeling Analyzer, running directly off the ontology, produces recommendations about the model itself rather than the data in it.

Components in Detail
Ontology Extractor — complete
Pulls an existing metamodel out of the Ardoq application through the Ontology API and emits it as an ontology. This is the fast path: where a customer has already invested in a metamodel, we can lift it directly with no interpretation step.

What it gives us is a faithful reflection of what is modelled. What it cannot give us is anything the customer knows but never encoded. This is what the Ontology Generator is for.

Ontology Generator — complete
Takes a corpus of system documentation (PDFs and similar) and builds an ontology from it using a two-agent loop:

Ontologist — proposes ontology structure from the source material.

Curator — reviews, challenges and refines the Ontologist's output, feeding corrections back around the loop.

This matters because documentation routinely contains constraints and goals that are not reflected in any metamodel: "every service must have a named owner", "these two systems must not exchange PII", "we are decommissioning this platform by Q3". Those statements are exactly the material a data quality check needs, and they exist only in prose. The Generator is how we get them into machine-usable form.

The Generator can also take the extracted ontology as input, so documentation-derived knowledge can be layered onto a metamodel-derived skeleton rather than built from nothing.

System Ontology — the hub
The consolidated artifact. Everything downstream reads it; nothing downstream talks to Ardoq or the documentation directly. Keeping a single, well-defined artifact in the middle is what lets us add consumers (like the EA Modeling Analyzer) without touching the producers.

Data Quality Analyzer — partially complete (POC)
Finds smells — patterns in the data that suggest a modeling or data-hygiene problem — and describes them in enough detail that they can be turned into executable checks.

Category Analyst reads the System Ontology and identifies candidate smell categories relevant to this particular model. Categories are derived from the ontology rather than drawn from a fixed list, so the checks are specific to the customer's model.

Each category is then handed to its own Curator/Ontologist pair, which works the category up into a concrete Smell Description grounded in the actual classes and properties of the ontology.

Categories are processed in parallel, and each pair receives the full System Ontology as context.

Current state: POC code, established prompts, generated outputs, and some manual evaluation of those outputs. The gap is in the ontologist loop, which is currently a single-shot agent, and in systematic evaluation — see open questions.

Query Generator — partially complete (POC)
Takes each Smell Description and, via a Query Conversion agent, produces an executable query that detects instances of that smell in the customer's data. The System Ontology is again supplied as context so the generated query uses real type and property names.

Current state: POC code, established prompts, generated outputs. Generated queries are currently Gremlin only.

Report Generator — testing
Collects the results of the generated queries and turns them into reports for a human audience. Building reports is available as a Python API, and executed via the AI wrapper on the report APIs in ardoq-api.

Current state: AI wrapper on the report APIs is merged into ardoq-api. The Python code is being tested.

Dashboard Generator — not started
Automates creating a Dashboard using a set of reports created by the Report Generator. Building Dashboards will require an AI wrapper on the dashboard APIs in ardoq-api.

EA Modeling Analyzer — not started
The other consumer of the System Ontology, and a different kind of output. Where the data quality chain asks "is the data wrong?", the Metamodel Analyst asks "is the model wrong?" — comparing the ontology against what good enterprise architecture modeling looks like and producing metamodel recommendations.

This is the component that most directly connects to the write-back path below: a recommendation about the metamodel is only fully useful if there is a way to act on it inside Ardoq.

GraphLake and the write-back path
Today the flow is one-directional: Ardoq → ontology → analysis. We expect to close the loop, folding descriptive ontologies back into the Ardoq application to update a metamodel.

Planning for this is currently paused, on purpose. Ardoq's storage layer is moving from PostgreSQL to GraphLake, an RDF database. The principals behind GraphLake have recently joined Ardoq, so the database's capabilities can be extended if and when we need them. Designing a write-back mechanism against the storage layer we are about to replace would be wasted effort; designing it against a native RDF store is substantially simpler, since the ontology and the stored data share a representation. The descriptive ontology may not completely match the internal modeling ontology for practical reasons, but we plan to provide automated mapping mechanisms to account for differences.

The practical consequence: the more ontology work we do now, the less translation work there is after the migration. The ontologies we build today are not throwaway scaffolding — they are the format the platform is moving toward.

Where we are focusing right now
We are re-evaluating the plan while engineering continues, with three questions in mind:

Are we building the right things in the right order? Producers are complete and consumers are at POC. Report Generator and EA Modeling Analyzer are both not started, and they serve very different audiences.

How do we evaluate quality? The Data Quality Analyzer has had manual evaluation only. We need a repeatable way to judge whether generated smells and queries are actually good.

How does this connect to the rest of Ardoq's AI work? Several teams are building agent capabilities. The System Ontology is a shared asset and we would rather it be reused than reinvented.

Glossary
Term

Meaning

Ontology

A formal, machine-readable description of the classes, relationships and constraints in a domain.

OWL

Web Ontology Language. A W3C standard for expressing ontologies; supports inheritance, cardinality and other constructs Ardoq's metamodel does not currently have.

RDF

Resource Description Framework. The W3C graph data model underlying OWL and GraphLake.

Metamodel

In Ardoq, the definition of component types, reference types and fields that shapes a customer's EA model.

Smell

A pattern in the data suggesting a modeling or data quality problem — borrowed from "code smell". Not necessarily an error, but worth a look.

System Ontology

The consolidated ontology for a given system, built from the Ardoq metamodel and/or its documentation. Input to all downstream analysis.

GraphLake

The RDF database Ardoq's storage layer is migrating to.

Curator / Ontologist

A paired-agent pattern used throughout: the Ontologist proposes, the Curator critiques, and the two iterate to a refined result.

addedLines: - augmentor: Implements a single, sharp, well-defined feature or change in an existing codebase with minimal blast radius, staying strictly in line with the codebase's established conventions. Use when you have ONE clearly-scoped addition or modification and want it done surgically. Give it the full spec plus any context you have already gathered; it will fetch whatever else it needs to understand the code. Do NOT use for broad, vague, or multi-feature work, or for anything that would force it to guess at requirements — it will refuse rather than assume. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash, LSP, NotebookEdit, WebFetch, WebSearch, TodoWrite)

- bugger: Finds and/or fixes bugs within a defined scope, according to orchestrator/user instructions. Operates in two dimensions. Trigger: either it's told about a specific bug (reproduce → find root cause → address it), or it's asked to scan a part of the code for latent bugs. Action: either propose solutions only (diagnosis + recommended fix, no code changed), or actually implement the fix. The instructions tell it which. When it writes fixes, they are surgical and adhere to the codebase's established standards. Use for debugging and bug-hunting; not for building new features. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash, LSP, NotebookEdit, WebFetch, WebSearch, TodoWrite)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- debloater: Reviews a specific piece of code or part of the codebase to remove bloat (dead code, redundancy, needless complexity) and improve logical organization, within a defined scope. Two action modes: IDENTIFY only (report the bloat and improvement opportunities it finds, changing nothing) or CLEAN (actually make the improvements). Under no circumstances does it make changes for their own sake — if nothing genuinely needs changing, it changes nothing and says so. Use for cleanup/tidying/simplification of existing code; not for adding features or fixing bugs. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash, LSP, NotebookEdit, WebFetch, WebSearch, TodoWrite)

- doccer: Documents code within a defined boundary — e.g. code an augmentor just wrote, a file/module/directory, or whatever the user points it at. Collects the context it needs, then writes documentation that matches the codebase's established documentation standards and/or the user's instructions (user instructions always win). Use when you want existing code documented without touching the code itself. It will NEVER modify code — not even to fix obvious bugs or errors; it only adds or edits documentation. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash, LSP, NotebookEdit, WebFetch, WebSearch, TodoWrite)

- enforcer: Scans code for (1) security issues and vulnerabilities and (2) violations of the codebase's conventions/standards, within a given scope — a specific file, a directory, or a global scan. Two action modes: REPORT only (surface findings to the user/orchestrator, change nothing) or FIX (apply the corrections surgically, conforming to established standards). Use for security review and convention/compliance enforcement. Not for adding features, general bug-hunting, or cleanup/refactoring for its own sake. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash, LSP, NotebookEdit, WebFetch, WebSearch, TodoWrite)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- merge-therapist: Resolves merge (or rebase/cherry-pick) conflicts and reports back a highly concise explanation of what it did. Default posture is the most harmonious resolution possible: preserve the intent and functionality of BOTH sides. If the user/orchestrator gives different instructions (prefer one side, drop something, take a specific shape), it follows those instead. Use when a merge/rebase leaves conflicted files, or when you want an in-progress conflict state untangled and explained. Not for doing the merge strategy planning, feature work, or bug-hunting beyond what conflict resolution requires. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash, LSP, NotebookEdit, TodoWrite)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- tester: Verifies that ONE specific, already-implemented feature or issue actually behaves the way it is supposed to. Give it (1) what the feature is and (2) what "working" looks like; it exercises the feature — reading code to orient, running curl/CLI/REPL calls, and writing throwaway ad-hoc tests in its own scratch environment — and reports whether the expected behavior holds, with evidence. It does NOT write unit tests into the repo, does NOT modify the codebase, and does NOT review code quality/conventions. Use to confirm a finished change does what it claims; not for building, fixing, or broad regression testing. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, LSP, WebFetch)

- gh-stack: Manage stacked branches and pull requests with the gh-stack GitHub CLI extension. Use when the user wants to create, push, rebase, sync, navigate, or view stacks of dependent PRs. Triggers on tasks involving stacked diffs, dependent pull requests, branch chains, or incremental code review workflows.
- implementation-plan: Produce a terse, fully-informed implementation plan for a specific piece of functionality — one that names exact files/layers/endpoints to touch, backed by having actually checked the code (including dependent/backend repos), with zero narrative clutter. Use when the user asks "lay out how we'd implement X", "what's the wiring needed for X", "give me an implementation plan", or similar — especially after a discussion has already established scope and the user wants the result distilled. NOT for exploratory "how does this work" mental-model requests (use mindmap for those), and NOT a substitute for actually writing the code.
- mindmap: Build a high-level, holistic conceptual map of how something in a codebase works — a whole codebase, a feature, a subsystem, a flow, or any specific thing the user points at. Use this when the user wants to *understand how something works* at an intuitive, big-picture level rather than a line-by-line walkthrough or a code edit. Triggers on requests like "explain how X works", "give me a mental model of", "how does this fit together", "map out", "I want to understand the architecture/flow of", "walk me through conceptually", "make sense of this codebase". NOT for making code changes, doing detailed code review, or answering a narrow factual lookup where a one-line answer suffices.
- tune: Extract the user's corrections and preferences from the current conversation and write them into the persistent behavioural instructions (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and the project memory directory). Use when the user says "tune", "update your instructions", "remember how I want you to work", "apply my feedback to your behaviour", or after a conversation where they corrected style, process, or output format. NOT for saving factual/project knowledge (that is ordinary memory) and NOT for one-off instructions that apply only to the current task.
- create-agent: Creates a new pydantic-ai agent for the Ardoq AI backend. Use when the user wants to add a new agent, build a new chat capability, or asks "create an agent for X".
- create-api: Creates a new API client function for calling ardoq-api endpoints. Use when adding backend integration, wrapping a Clojure endpoint, or when user asks "create an API for X".
- create-postmortem: Writes a post-mortem markdown file under docs/post-mortems/ and publishes it to Confluence (AIP space, "Post Mortems" parent). Use when the user wants to document an incident, write a post-mortem, or RCA.
- create-tool: Creates a new tool function for AI agents. Use when the user wants to add a tool, create a data fetching function, or asks "create a tool for X".
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

from ardoq_ai.api.reports.api import report_search
from ardoq_ai.tools.ardoq_tool.tool_decorator import ToolLimit, ardoq_tool
from ardoq_ai.tools.gremlin.schema import GremlinExecutionResult


@ardoq_tool(
    limit=ToolLimit(
        max_invocations=4,
        limit_exceeded_message=(
            "You have reached the maximum of 4 validate_gremlin_query calls. "
            "Return your best query so far, or set unsupported=true if you could not build a valid query."
        ),
    )
)
async def validate_gremlin_query(
    workspace_ids: list[str],
    query: str,
) -> GremlinExecutionResult:
    """Validate a generated Gremlin query by running a 5-row preview.

    Use this to validate that your generated gremlin query is correct before
    returning it as the final answer. The results are limited to 5 rows to
    keep the response small.

    You may call this tool at most 4 times per agent run. Use attempts wisely.

    Check the results to verify:
    - The query doesn't error (syntax issues, invalid properties, etc.)
    - It returns rows (not 0 results, which may indicate wrong edge direction or filter)
    - The columns and values look correct for what the user asked

    If the query errors, fix the syntax and retry (counts as an attempt).
    If results look correct, return the query immediately — do not re-validate.
    If 0 results and no clear fix, return the query anyway — the data may simply not match.

    Args:
        workspace_ids: The workspace ids to scope the query to.
        query: A valid Gremlin traversal string (e.g., "g.V().hasLabel('Application')")

    Returns:
        GremlinExecutionResult with row count, columns, and preview rows.
    """
    data = await report_search(query=query, workspace_ids=workspace_ids, size=5)

    results = data.results
    total_rows = data.total_number_of_rows if data.total_number_of_rows else len(results)

    # Only include columns when there are actual results.
    # The API returns all possible columns even for 0 results,
    # which wastes tokens and confuses the agent.
    columns = [col.key for col in data.columns] if results else []

    return GremlinExecutionResult(
        total_rows=total_rows,
        columns=columns,
        preview_rows=results[:5],
    )

@ardoq_tool(features=[ArdoqFeature.ONTOLOGY])
async def get_ontology(
    model: str | None = None,
) -> OntologyGetOutput:
    """Fetch the OWL ontology for the organisation in DLe (Description Logic expression) syntax.

    The ontology is a formal, machine-readable description of the organisation's metamodel:
    the component types, reference types, fields, and their relationships, expressed as OWL
    classes and properties. It gives a complete structural picture of what kinds of entities
    exist in the Ardoq model and how they relate to one another.

    Use this tool when you need to understand the organisation's metamodel at a structural
    level — for example, to interpret component type names, discover what field types and
    enumerations exist, or reason about how entity types relate.  Prefer the metamodel tools
    (e.g. get_metamodel_fields) when you only need field definitions or type lists, since they
    return lighter, more targeted data.

    Args:
        model: Optional model ID to restrict the ontology to a single metamodel.
            Useful when the organisation has multiple models and you only need the
            schema for one of them.  When omitted, the full org-level ontology is
            returned, covering all models.

    Returns:
        ontology: The OWL ontology as a DLe string, with blank lines removed for
            compactness.  Declares all component types as OWL classes, all reference
            types as object properties, and all fields as data properties, together
            with their domain, range, and any enumeration constraints.
    """
    result = await ontology_get(model=model)
    return OntologyGetOutput(ontology=result)

    return data["document"]

########## agents/ai_query_builder/agent.py
import json

from pydantic_ai import RunContext

from ardoq_ai.agents.ai_query_builder.schema import (
    AiQueryBuilderDependencies,
    DslAgentOutput,
)
from ardoq_ai.agents.base import ArdoqAgent
from ardoq_ai.agents.prompts.data_context import DATA_TAG_WARNING
from ardoq_ai.agents.prompts.declining import DECLINE_GRACEFULLY
from ardoq_ai.config.deployments import ModelId, get_llm_config
from ardoq_ai.tools.components.functions import search_components_by_workspace
from ardoq_ai.utils.prompt_utils import wrap_in_data_tag

ai_query_builder_agent = ArdoqAgent(
    name="ai_query_builder_agent",
    deps_type=AiQueryBuilderDependencies,
    tools=[search_components_by_workspace],
    output_type=DslAgentOutput,
    model_settings=get_llm_config(ModelId.CLAUDE_SONNET_4_6, temperature=0.1),
)


@ai_query_builder_agent.instructions
async def get_system_prompt(ctx: RunContext[AiQueryBuilderDependencies]) -> str:
    """Build the system prompt from the pre-fetched workspace context."""
    context = ctx.deps.context
    component_types_json = json.dumps(context.component_types)
    reference_lines: list[str] = []
    for rt in context.reference_triples:
        reference_lines.append(
            f"- `{rt.source_type}` --[`{rt.reference_type}`]--> `{rt.target_type}`\n"
            f'    Filtering {rt.source_type}: operator "to", referenceTypeName "{rt.reference_type}"\n'
            f'    Filtering {rt.target_type}: operator "from", referenceTypeName "{rt.reference_type}"'
        )
    reference_triples_str = "\n".join(reference_lines)
    custom_fields_json = json.dumps([cf.model_dump(exclude_none=True) for cf in context.custom_fields])

    return f"""You convert natural language queries to Ardoq search filters.
You will be given a user query, and you should respond with only valid JSON in the response format specified below.

Workspace ids in scope: {ctx.deps.workspace_ids}. Scope all lookups to these workspaces.

{DATA_TAG_WARNING}

## Response Format

When the query is supported:
{{
  "query": {{ /* Query */ }},
  "unsupported": false
}}

When the query is unsupported, provide an empty query (never use null for the query field):
{{
  "query": {{"condition": "AND", "rules": []}},
  "unsupported": true,
  "unsupportedCategory": "string", // category of why query is unsupported
  "reason": "string" // Short, friendly message for the end user. See "Writing the reason" below.
}}

## Writing the reason

The `reason` is shown directly to a non-technical user as an inline error.

{DECLINE_GRACEFULLY}

Call the feature "Advanced Search", never "DSL". Avoid query-language jargon ("DSL", "operator", "aggregation", "traversal").

Good: "Advanced Search can't rank components by how many connections they have. Try filtering on a specific field instead."
Good: "Advanced Search can't filter on a connected component's fields."

## Unsupported Categories

When a query is unsupported, categorize it using one of these categories:

- **references** - Complex reference relationships that cannot be expressed with available operators
- **unclear_query** - User query is ambiguous or lacks necessary details to construct a filter
- **missing_field** - Query references a field that doesn't exist in common or custom fields
- **unsupported_operator** - Query requires an operator that is not available for the field type
- **complex_logic** - Query logic is too complex to express in the available query structure
- **invalid_query** - Query references invalid values (e.g., non-existent component types, invalid date formats, wrong reference types)
- **error** - General parsing or processing error

Choose the most specific category that matches the reason for being unsupported.

## Query Structure

{{
  "condition": "AND" | "OR",
  "rules": [ /* Rule or nested Query */ ]
}}

- "AND" = all rules must match
- "OR" = at least one must match
- rules can contain Rule objects or nested SubQuery objects for complex logic. Any rule type (including reference rules) can appear inside any AND/OR condition. Try to go for simpler queries to achieve the user's question

## Rule Structure

{{
  "id": "<field-name>",
  "field": "<field-name>",
  "type": "string" | "date" | "number" | "boolean",
  "input": "text",
  "operator": "<operator>",
  "value": <value>
}}

## Operators

Exact match:
  equal, not_equal

Text search:
  contains, not_contains - case-insensitive eg. "app" matches "App", "application", "Pineapple"
  contains_substring, not_contains_substring - partial text match

Null checks: You can use these for checking if a value is set or not set for strings, booleans and numbers
  is_empty, is_not_empty

Comparisons (numbers & dates):
  greater, less, equal, between (P.S for between the value should be an array in format ["start", "end"])

Reference directions:
  to, from - used for filtering by references between components

## Possible Values

These are the possible value types

| null // for operator Operator.IS_EMPTY and Operator.IS_NOT_EMPTY
| string
| boolean
| number
| [string, string] // date with "between" operator

## Common Fields
You have the following common fields that are common to all components.
You will also be provided a set of custom fields that are custom to the workspace that the user is looking at and may be referenced in their query

String fields:
   _id - Item ID
  name - component name
  description - the description of the component
  created-by - The ID of the user who created the component
  last-modified-by
  parent - Use is_empty/is_not_empty to check if component has a parent. Use equal with a component ID to filter by specific parent.

Number fields:
  child-count - Number of direct child components

Date fields:
  created - The date the component was created
  last-updated - The date the component was last updated

Component type:
    typeName - This is the component type that the user is referring to
    {wrap_in_data_tag(f"The list of available component types (typeName) are {component_types_json}", "component-types")}

## References

References represent relationships between components. There are two types of reference filters:

### Simple Reference Filters

Use these to filter by the presence or absence of a reference type, regardless of what it connects to:

**has-outgoing-reference-type** - Component has an outgoing reference of this type
**does-not-have-outgoing-reference-type** - Component lacks an outgoing reference of this type
**has-incoming-reference-type** - Component has an incoming reference of this type
**does-not-have-incoming-reference-type** - Component lacks an incoming reference of this type

Simple reference rule structure:
{{
  "id": "has-outgoing-reference-type" | "does-not-have-outgoing-reference-type" | "has-incoming-reference-type" | "does-not-have-incoming-reference-type",
  "field": "has-outgoing-reference-type" | "does-not-have-outgoing-reference-type" | "has-incoming-reference-type" | "does-not-have-incoming-reference-type",
  "input": "text",
  "type": "string",
  "operator": "equal",
  "value": "<reference-type-name>"
}}

- **value**: The reference type name (e.g., "Owns", "Accesses", "Supplies", "Implicit")

### Complex Reference Filters

Use these to filter by relationships to and from specific component types:

**has-reference** - Find components that have a reference to another component type
**has-no-reference** - Find components that do NOT have a reference to another component type

You should be only using these complex references if the value you're pointing to was explicitly mentioned in the query.
Do not make up a component-type for a value just because it's in the list of component types.
**When to use component search vs component-type filtering:**
- **Specific entity by name**: ALWAYS search for the component by name to find its ID, then use targetEntityType "component". Try different search variants if the first attempt doesn't match.
- **Generic type reference**: If the user refers generically to one of the component types listed above, use targetEntityType "component-type" with the type name directly.

**Limitations** (mark these as unsupported with category "references"):

##### reference_agent.py
import json

from pydantic_ai import RunContext

from ardoq_ai.agents.ai_query_builder.schema import AiQueryBuilderDependencies, GremlinBuilderOutput
from ardoq_ai.agents.base import ArdoqAgent
from ardoq_ai.agents.prompts.declining import DECLINE_GRACEFULLY
from ardoq_ai.config.deployments import ModelId, get_llm_config
from ardoq_ai.tools.components.functions import search_components_by_workspace
from ardoq_ai.tools.gremlin.toolset import build_gremlin_toolset
from ardoq_ai.utils.prompt_utils import wrap_in_data_tag

reference_gremlin_agent = ArdoqAgent(
    name="reference_gremlin_agent",
    deps_type=AiQueryBuilderDependencies,
    tools=[search_components_by_workspace],
    toolsets=[build_gremlin_toolset()],
    output_type=GremlinBuilderOutput,
    model_settings=get_llm_config(ModelId.CLAUDE_SONNET_4_6, temperature=0.1),
)


@reference_gremlin_agent.instructions
async def get_system_prompt(ctx: RunContext[AiQueryBuilderDependencies]) -> str:
    """Build the system prompt from the pre-fetched workspace context."""
    deps = ctx.deps
    context = deps.context
    component_types_str = ", ".join(f"`{ct}`" for ct in context.component_types)

    reference_lines: list[str] = [
        f"- `{rt.source_type}` --[`{rt.reference_type}`]--> `{rt.target_type}`\n"
        f"    From {rt.source_type}: `.out('{rt.reference_type}')` → reaches {rt.target_type}\n"
        f"    From {rt.target_type}: `.in('{rt.reference_type}')` → reaches {rt.source_type}"
        for rt in context.reference_triples
    ]
    reference_triples_str = "\n".join(reference_lines)

    custom_fields_json = json.dumps([cf.model_dump(exclude_none=True) for cf in context.custom_fields])

    return f"""You are a Gremlin query generator for Apache TinkerPop 3.7.
You specialize in queries that filter components based on properties of referenced components — "one-step-out" queries.

Workspace ids in scope: {deps.workspace_ids}. Scope all lookups to these workspaces.

---

## YOUR SCOPE

You handle "one-step-out" reference queries: the user wants to find components of one type, filtered by properties on a component one reference away.

Only one-step-out. No advanced `project()`/`select()` gremlin. No multi-hop traversals (A → B → C). No aggregations, grouping, hierarchy, paths, or statistics.

Use whatever gremlin constructs make sense to express the query correctly within this scope. Use your judgment.

---

## EDGE DIRECTION

Schema: `Source --[Edge]--> Target`
- `.out('Edge')` = follow the arrow (Source → Target)
- `.in('Edge')` = against the arrow (Target ← Source)

**Always trust the schema directions below. Do not guess.**

---

## COMMON MISTAKES TO AVOID

### 1. Wrong component type name
If your first query returns 0 results, the most likely cause is a wrong component type label — not edge direction. Check the schema below first.

### 2. Missing type guard after traversal if the user asked for a specific type
```
// WRONG: .where(__.out('Accesses'))
// RIGHT: .where(__.out('Accesses').hasLabel('Database'))
```

### 3. Using `.in` without `__` prefix in nested context
`in` is a Python reserved word. Always use `__.in()` inside `.where()`, `.not()`, `.filter()`.

---

## EXAMPLES

"Applications owned by business capabilities with high importance"
```
g.V().hasLabel('Application').where(__.in('Owns').hasLabel('Business Capability').has('importance', 'high'))
```

"Servers hosting deprecated applications"
```
g.V().hasLabel('Server').where(__.out('Hosts').hasLabel('Application').has('status', 'deprecated'))
```

"Databases NOT accessed by any application"
```
g.V().hasLabel('Database').not(__.in('Accesses').hasLabel('Application'))
```

"Applications with name containing 'Portal' owned by a Person named 'John'"
```
g.V().hasLabel('Application').has('name', TextP.containing('Portal')).where(__.in('Owns').hasLabel('Person').has('name', 'John'))
```

---

## OUT OF SCOPE — MARK AS UNSUPPORTED

If the query requires aggregations, projections, multi-hop traversals, hierarchy, paths, or statistics — set `unsupported: true` and write the `reason` per "Writing the reason" below.
If it's genuinely about filtering components by a referenced component's properties, handle it.

---

## SCHEMA

### Component Types (vertex labels)
{wrap_in_data_tag(component_types_str, "component-types")}

### Edges (reference triples)
{wrap_in_data_tag(reference_triples_str, "reference-triples")}

### Custom Fields
{wrap_in_data_tag(custom_fields_json, "custom-fields")}

---

## FILTERING BY SPECIFIC COMPONENTS

When the user mentions a specific component by name (e.g., "Finance", "London", "Portal"):
1. **Always search for the component by name first** to find the actual component and confirm its exact name.
2. Then use `.has('name', '<exact confirmed name>')` with the confirmed name.
3. Do NOT guess names or use partial matches like `TextP.containing()` for specific entities.

Only use `TextP.containing()` when the user explicitly asks for a substring/partial match (e.g., "name containing...").

Do NOT use `_id` fields — they may not resolve correctly in gremlin graph traversals.

---

## QUERY EXECUTION

Always use `validate_gremlin_query` to validate your query before returning it.

**You have a maximum of 4 execution attempts total. Use them wisely.**

**Workflow:**
1. Generate your gremlin query using the schema below — trust it for edge directions
2. Call `validate_gremlin_query` to test it
3. If explicit error → fix syntax or wrong component type name and retry (counts as attempt)
4. If 0 results → **this may be correct** — the data may simply not match. Only retry if you have a clear reason (e.g., you used a wrong component type name). Do NOT run discovery queries.
5. If results look correct → return the query

**Do not run exploration queries** like `outE().label().dedup()`. The schema already tells you the edge directions. Trust it.

---

## OUTPUT

Return the gremlin query string in the `query` field.
If the query is out of scope, set `unsupported: true` and write the `reason` per "Writing the reason" below.

---

## Writing the reason

The `reason` is shown directly to a non-technical user as an inline error.

{DECLINE_GRACEFULLY}

Call the feature "Advanced Search". Avoid query-language jargon ("Gremlin", "traversal", "aggregation", "one step out").

Good: "Advanced Search can't rank components by how many connections they have. Try filtering on a specific field instead."
Good: "Advanced Search can't filter on a connected component's fields."
"""
##### schema.py
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, SerializerFunctionWrapHandler, model_serializer

from ardoq_ai.api.generated.models import AiQueryBuilderContext


class DslRule(BaseModel):
    """A single rule in the Advanced Search DSL."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True, frozen=True, serialize_by_alias=True)
    id: str
    field: str
    type: str
    input: str = "text"
    operator: str
    value: str | int | float | bool | list[str] | None = None
    # Optional fields for reference rules
    target_entity_type: str | None = Field(
        validation_alias="targetEntityType", serialization_alias="targetEntityType", default=None
    )
    reference_type_name: str | None = Field(
        validation_alias="referenceTypeName", serialization_alias="referenceTypeName", default=None
    )

    @model_serializer(mode="wrap")
    def _exclude_none(self, handler: SerializerFunctionWrapHandler) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {k: v for k, v in handler(self).items() if v is not None or k == "value"}


class DslQuery(BaseModel):
    """A query with condition and rules (rules can be DslRule or nested DslQuery)."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True, frozen=True, serialize_by_alias=True)
    condition: Literal["AND", "OR"]
    rules: list["DslRule | DslQuery"]


class UnsupportedCategory(str, Enum):
    """Categories for why a query is unsupported."""

    REFERENCES = "references"
    UNCLEAR_QUERY = "unclear_query"
    MISSING_FIELD = "missing_field"
    UNSUPPORTED_OPERATOR = "unsupported_operator"
    COMPLEX_LOGIC = "complex_logic"
    INVALID_QUERY = "invalid_query"
    ERROR = "error"


class AiQueryBuilderDependencies(BaseModel):
    """Dependencies for the AI Query Builder agent.

    Carries the pre-fetched workspace context so that neither the DSL agent nor the
    gremlin agent makes its own API call to fetch it.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    workspace_ids: list[str] = []
    gremlin_fallback_enabled: bool = False
    context: AiQueryBuilderContext


class GremlinBuilderOutput(BaseModel):
    """Structured output from the reference gremlin agent."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True, frozen=True, serialize_by_alias=True)

    query: str | None = None
    unsupported: bool = False
    reason: str | None = None
    unsupported_category: UnsupportedCategory | None = Field(
        validation_alias="unsupportedCategory", serialization_alias="unsupportedCategory", default=None
    )


class DslAgentOutput(BaseModel):
    """What the DSL agent LLM produces."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True, serialize_by_alias=True)

    query: DslQuery | None = None
    unsupported: bool = False
    reason: str | None = None
    unsupported_category: UnsupportedCategory | None = Field(
        validation_alias="unsupportedCategory", serialization_alias="unsupportedCategory", default=None
    )


class QueryBuilderOutput(DslAgentOutput):
    """Final API response. Extends DslAgentOutput with gremlin fallback fields."""

    query_type: Literal["dsl", "gremlin"] = Field(
        validation_alias="queryType", serialization_alias="queryType", default="dsl"
    )
    gremlin_query: str | None = Field(validation_alias="gremlinQuery", serialization_alias="gremlinQuery", default=None)
##### utils.py
from ardoq_ai.agents.ai_query_builder.schema import DslQuery, DslRule
from ardoq_ai.api.generated.models import ReferenceTriple


def find_type_name(rules: list[DslRule | DslQuery]) -> str | None:
    """Find the typeName value from direct (non-nested) rules in a group."""
    for rule in rules:
        if isinstance(rule, DslRule) and rule.field == "typeName" and isinstance(rule.value, str):
            return rule.value
    return None


def is_complex_reference(rule: DslRule) -> bool:
    """Check if a rule is a complex reference rule (has-reference / has-no-reference)."""
    return bool(rule.reference_type_name and rule.operator in ("to", "from"))


def fix_reference_rule(
    rule: DslRule,
    type_name: str | None,
    triples: list[ReferenceTriple],
) -> tuple[DslRule, str | None]:
    """Validate and fix a single reference rule against known triples.

    Uses the LLM's chosen operator as a signal for which triple it intended.
    Only overrides the operator when the LLM's direction is impossible.

    Returns (possibly_fixed_rule, optional_issue).
    """
    if type_name is None:
        return rule, None

    matching = [t for t in triples if t.reference_type == rule.reference_type_name]
    if not matching:
        return rule, f"LLM hallucinated reference type '{rule.reference_type_name}'"

    # "to" means primary entity is source, "from" means primary entity is target
    if rule.operator == "to":
        intended = next((t for t in matching if t.source_type == type_name), None)
    else:
        intended = next((t for t in matching if t.target_type == type_name), None)

    if intended is not None:
        return rule, None

    if rule.operator == "to":
        opposite = next((t for t in matching if t.target_type == type_name), None)
        correct_op = "from"
    else:
        opposite = next((t for t in matching if t.source_type == type_name), None)
        correct_op = "to"

            id=rule.id,
            field=rule.field,
            type=rule.type,
            input=rule.input,
            operator=correct_op,
            value=rule.value,
            target_entity_type=rule.target_entity_type,
            reference_type_name=rule.reference_type_name,
        ),
        None,
    )


def fix_query_references(
    query: DslQuery,
    triples: list[ReferenceTriple],

    At each group, finds the in-scope typeName (from sibling rules or parent),

    - Everything else → pass through

    type_name = (find_type_name(query.rules) if query.condition == "AND" else None) or parent_type_name

        elif is_complex_reference(rule):

            new_rules.append(fixed_rule)
            if issue:
                issues.append(issue)
        else:
            new_rules.append(rule)

    return DslQuery(condition=query.condition, rules=new_rules), issues

You handle "one-step-out" reference queries: the user wants to find components of one type, filtered by properties on a component one reference away.

Schema: `Source --[Edge]--> Target`

- `.in('Edge')` = against the arrow (Target ← Source)

g.V().hasLabel('Application').where(__.in('Owns').hasLabel('Business Capability').has('importance', 'high'))

g.V().hasLabel('Database').not(__.in('Accesses').hasLabel('Application'))

##### query_builder_pipeline.py
"""Query Builder pipeline.

Orchestrates the full query builder flow as an explicit sequence of typed steps:

  1. fetch_context       — fetch workspace context once (component types, reference triples, custom fields)
  2. run_dsl_agent       — run the DSL agent with the pre-fetched context
  3. fix_references      — deterministic post-processing: fix wrong reference directions, mark unresolvable ones unsupported
  4. maybe_gremlin       — if DSL returned unsupported/references and gremlin is enabled, fall back to the gremlin agent
  5. wrap_component_type — wrap a successful DSL query in the required top-level AND + type=component rule
"""

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

from ardoq_ai.agents.ai_query_builder.agent import ai_query_builder_agent
from ardoq_ai.agents.ai_query_builder.reference_agent import reference_gremlin_agent
from ardoq_ai.agents.ai_query_builder.schema import (
    AiQueryBuilderDependencies,
    DslAgentOutput,
    DslQuery,
    DslRule,
    QueryBuilderOutput,
    UnsupportedCategory,
)
from ardoq_ai.agents.ai_query_builder.utils import fix_query_references
from ardoq_ai.agents.default.models import get_shared_completion_client
from ardoq_ai.api.ai_query_builder.api import get_ai_query_builder_context
from ardoq_ai.completion.non_streaming import run_completion
from ardoq_ai.completion.schemas.message import Message
from ardoq_ai.pipeline.core.exceptions import PipelineStepError
from ardoq_ai.pipeline.core.pipeline import pipe
from ardoq_ai.pipeline.core.steps.function import function_step

COMPONENT_TYPE_RULE = DslRule(
    id="type", field="type", type="string", input="select", operator="equal", value="component"
)


class QueryBuilderPipelineCtx(BaseModel):
    """Pipeline context — immutable, available to every step."""

    workspace_ids: list[str]
    user_query: str
    gremlin_fallback_enabled: bool = False


class DslResultBundle(BaseModel):
    """Carries the DSL agent output + the deps (which hold the pre-fetched context) forward."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, arbitrary_types_allowed=True)

    output: DslAgentOutput
    deps: AiQueryBuilderDependencies


# --- Pipeline steps ---


async def fetch_context(
    input: QueryBuilderPipelineCtx,
    ctx: QueryBuilderPipelineCtx,
) -> AiQueryBuilderDependencies:
    """Fetch workspace context once and inject it into deps.

    All subsequent steps receive deps with context already set,
    so neither the DSL agent nor the gremlin agent will re-fetch it.
    """
    context = await get_ai_query_builder_context(workspace_ids=ctx.workspace_ids)
    return AiQueryBuilderDependencies(
        workspace_ids=ctx.workspace_ids,
        gremlin_fallback_enabled=ctx.gremlin_fallback_enabled,
        context=context,
    )


async def run_dsl_agent(
    deps: AiQueryBuilderDependencies,
    ctx: QueryBuilderPipelineCtx,
) -> DslResultBundle:
    """Run the DSL agent. The agent uses deps.context instead of fetching."""
    result = await run_completion(
        new_message=Message(type="message", role="user", content=ctx.user_query),
        agent=ai_query_builder_agent,
        model=get_shared_completion_client(),
        dependencies=deps,
    )
    if result.status != "success":
        raise PipelineStepError(cause=Exception(result.error.message), step_name="run_dsl_agent")
    return DslResultBundle(output=result.output, deps=deps)


def fix_references(
    input: DslResultBundle,
    ctx: QueryBuilderPipelineCtx,
) -> DslResultBundle:
    """Fix wrong reference directions; mark unresolvable reference combinations as unsupported.

    Uses the pre-fetched context from deps — no API call.
    """
    if input.output.unsupported or input.output.query is None:
        return input

    context = input.deps.context
    if not context.reference_triples:
        return input

    fixed_query, issues = fix_query_references(input.output.query, context.reference_triples)

    if issues:
        return DslResultBundle(
            output=DslAgentOutput(
                query=None,
                unsupported=True,
                reason="This query involves references that can't be expressed as a single search. Try simplifying or breaking it into separate queries.",
                unsupported_category=UnsupportedCategory.REFERENCES,
            ),
            deps=input.deps,
        )

    return DslResultBundle(
        output=DslAgentOutput(
            query=fixed_query,
            unsupported=False,
            reason=input.output.reason,
            unsupported_category=input.output.unsupported_category,
        ),
        deps=input.deps,
    )


async def maybe_gremlin(
    input: DslResultBundle,
    ctx: QueryBuilderPipelineCtx,
) -> QueryBuilderOutput:
    """Fall back to the gremlin agent when DSL returned unsupported/references.

    Passes the same pre-fetched context in deps, so the gremlin agent
    won't make a third API call for workspace context.
    """
    output = input.output

    if not (output.unsupported and output.unsupported_category == UnsupportedCategory.REFERENCES):
        return QueryBuilderOutput(**output.model_dump())

    if not ctx.gremlin_fallback_enabled:
        return QueryBuilderOutput(**output.model_dump())

    gremlin_result = await run_completion(
        new_message=Message(type="message", role="user", content=ctx.user_query),
        agent=reference_gremlin_agent,
        model=get_shared_completion_client(),
        dependencies=input.deps,
    )
    if gremlin_result.status != "success":
        raise PipelineStepError(cause=Exception(gremlin_result.error.message), step_name="maybe_gremlin")
    gremlin_output = gremlin_result.output
    if gremlin_output.unsupported:
        return QueryBuilderOutput(
            unsupported=True,
            reason=gremlin_output.reason,
            unsupported_category=gremlin_output.unsupported_category or UnsupportedCategory.REFERENCES,
        )

    return QueryBuilderOutput(
        query_type="gremlin",
        gremlin_query=gremlin_output.query,
        unsupported=False,
    )


def wrap_component_type(
    input: QueryBuilderOutput,
    ctx: QueryBuilderPipelineCtx,
) -> QueryBuilderOutput:
    """Wrap a successful DSL query in the required top-level AND + type=component rule.

    No-op for gremlin results (query is None) and unsupported responses.
    """
    if input.query is None or input.unsupported or input.query_type == "gremlin":
        return input

    return QueryBuilderOutput(
        query=DslQuery(condition="AND", rules=[COMPONENT_TYPE_RULE, input.query]),
        unsupported=input.unsupported,
        reason=input.reason,
        unsupported_category=input.unsupported_category,
    )


query_builder_pipeline = pipe(
    "query_builder",
    function_step(fetch_context),
    function_step(run_dsl_agent),
    function_step(fix_references),
    function_step(maybe_gremlin),
    function_step(wrap_component_type),
)

def get_discriminator(v: Any):
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return v.get("pipelineType") or v.get("pipeline_type")
    return getattr(v, "pipeline_type", None)


class BasePipelineRequest(BaseModel):
    thread_id: str | None = Field(alias="threadId", default=None)


class QueryBuilderPipelineRequest(BasePipelineRequest):
    pipeline_type: Literal["query_builder"] = Field("query_builder", alias="pipelineType")
    workspace_ids: list[str] = Field(alias="workspaceIds")
    user_query: str = Field(alias="userQuery")
    gremlin_fallback_enabled: bool = Field(alias="gremlinFallbackEnabled", default=False)


class InsightsPipelineRequest(BasePipelineRequest):
    pipeline_type: Literal["insights"] = Field("insights", alias="pipelineType")
    report_id: str = Field(alias="reportId")


PipelineRequest = Annotated[
    Annotated[QueryBuilderPipelineRequest, Tag("query_builder")] | Annotated[InsightsPipelineRequest, Tag("insights")],

    All subsequent steps receive deps with context already set,
    so neither the DSL agent nor the gremlin agent will re-fetch it.
    """
    context = await get_ai_query_builder_context(workspace_ids=ctx.workspace_ids)
    return AiQueryBuilderDependencies(
        workspace_ids=ctx.workspace_ids,
        gremlin_fallback_enabled=ctx.gremlin_fallback_enabled,
        context=context,
    )


async def run_dsl_agent(
    deps: AiQueryBuilderDependencies,
    ctx: QueryBuilderPipelineCtx,
) -> DslResultBundle:
    """Run the DSL agent. The agent uses deps.context instead of fetching."""
    result = await run_completion(
        new_message=Message(type="message", role="user", content=ctx.user_query),
        agent=ai_query_builder_agent,
        model=get_shared_completion_client(),
        dependencies=deps,
    )
    if result.status != "success":
        raise PipelineStepError(cause=Exception(result.error.message), step_name="run_dsl_agent")
    return DslResultBundle(output=result.output, deps=deps)


def fix_references(
    input: DslResultBundle,
    ctx: QueryBuilderPipelineCtx,
) -> DslResultBundle:
    """Fix wrong reference directions; mark unresolvable reference combinations as unsupported.

    Uses the pre-fetched context from deps — no API call.
    """
    if input.output.unsupported or input.output.query is None:
        return input

    context = input.deps.context
    if not context.reference_triples:
        return input

    fixed_query, issues = fix_query_references(input.output.query, context.reference_triples)

    if issues:
        return DslResultBundle(
            output=DslAgentOutput(
                query=None,
                unsupported=True,
                reason="This query involves references that can't be expressed as a single search. Try simplifying or breaking it into separate queries.",
                unsupported_category=UnsupportedCategory.REFERENCES,
            ),
            deps=input.deps,
        )

    return DslResultBundle(
        output=DslAgentOutput(
            query=fixed_query,
            unsupported=False,
            reason=input.output.reason,
            unsupported_category=input.output.unsupported_category,
        ),
        deps=input.deps,
    )


async def maybe_gremlin(
    input: DslResultBundle,
    ctx: QueryBuilderPipelineCtx,
) -> QueryBuilderOutput:
    """Fall back to the gremlin agent when DSL returned unsupported/references.

    Passes the same pre-fetched context in deps, so the gremlin agent
    won't make a third API call for workspace context.
    """
    output = input.output

    if not (output.unsupported and output.unsupported_category == UnsupportedCategory.REFERENCES):
        return QueryBuilderOutput(**output.model_dump())

    if not ctx.gremlin_fallback_enabled:
        return QueryBuilderOutput(**output.model_dump())

    gremlin_result = await run_completion(
        new_message=Message(type="message", role="user", content=ctx.user_query),
        agent=reference_gremlin_agent,
        model=get_shared_completion_client(),
        dependencies=input.deps,
    )
    if gremlin_result.status != "success":
        raise PipelineStepError(cause=Exception(gremlin_result.error.message), step_name="maybe_gremlin")
    gremlin_output = gremlin_result.output
    if gremlin_output.unsupported:
        return QueryBuilderOutput(
            unsupported=True,
            reason=gremlin_output.reason,
            unsupported_category=gremlin_output.unsupported_category or UnsupportedCategory.REFERENCES,
        )

    return QueryBuilderOutput(
        query_type="gremlin",
        gremlin_query=gremlin_output.query,
        unsupported=False,
    )


def wrap_component_type(
    input: QueryBuilderOutput,
    ctx: QueryBuilderPipelineCtx,
) -> QueryBuilderOutput:
    """Wrap a successful DSL query in the required top-level AND + type=component rule.

    No-op for gremlin results (query is None) and unsupported responses.
    """
    if input.query is None or input.unsupported or input.query_type == "gremlin":
        return input

    return QueryBuilderOutput(
        query=DslQuery(condition="AND", rules=[COMPONENT_TYPE_RULE, input.query]),
        unsupported=input.unsupported,
        reason=input.reason,
        unsupported_category=input.unsupported_category,
    )


query_builder_pipeline = pipe(
    "query_builder",
    function_step(fetch_context),
    function_step(run_dsl_agent),
    function_step(fix_references),
    function_step(maybe_gremlin),
    function_step(wrap_component_type),
)

async def run_pipeline_response(
    request: PipelineRequest,
) -> PipelineResponseSuccess[BaseModel] | PipelineResponseFailure:
    """Run a pipeline to completion and return the typed final output.

    Args:
        request: The pipeline request selecting which pipeline to run and its inputs.

    Returns:
        PipelineResponseSuccess on success, containing the pipeline's typed final_output.
        PipelineResponseFailure on PipelineStepError, containing the failing step name and error.
    """
    ctx = get_request_ctx()
    logger = ctx.logger
    metadata = require_api(ctx).authorization.metadata

    tracing_metadata = {
        **(request.model_dump(exclude={"thread_id"})),
        **(metadata.model_dump() if metadata is not None else {}),
    }

    async with request_trace_context(
        name=request.pipeline_type,
        thread_id=request.thread_id,
        metadata=tracing_metadata,
    ):
        try:
            output = await run_pipeline(request)
            return PipelineResponseSuccess(final_output=output)
        except PipelineStepError as e:
            logger.exception(f"Pipeline step failed: {e.step_name}")
            return PipelineResponseFailure(step_name=e.step_name, error=str(e.cause))


async def run_pipeline(request: PipelineRequest) -> BaseModel:
    """Dispatch to the appropriate pipeline's execute() based on request type."""
    match request:
        case QueryBuilderPipelineRequest():
            ctx = QueryBuilderPipelineCtx(
                workspace_ids=request.workspace_ids,
                user_query=request.user_query,
                gremlin_fallback_enabled=request.gremlin_fallback_enabled,
            )
            return await query_builder_pipeline.execute(ctx, ctx)

        case InsightsPipelineRequest():
            insights_ctx = InsightsPipelineCtx(
                report_id=request.report_id,
            )
            return await insights_pipeline.execute(insights_ctx, insights_ctx)

        case _ as unreachable:
            assert_never(unreachable)

    InsightsPipelineRequest,
    PipelineRequest,
    QueryBuilderPipelineRequest,
)
from src.api.domain.responses.pipeline_response import (
    PipelineResponseFailure,
    PipelineResponseSuccess,
)


async def run_pipeline_response(
    request: PipelineRequest,
) -> PipelineResponseSuccess[BaseModel] | PipelineResponseFailure:
    """Run a pipeline to completion and return the typed final output.

    Args:
        request: The pipeline request selecting which pipeline to run and its inputs.

    Returns:
        PipelineResponseSuccess on success, containing the pipeline's typed final_output.
        PipelineResponseFailure on PipelineStepError, containing the failing step name and error.
    """
    ctx = get_request_ctx()
    logger = ctx.logger
    metadata = require_api(ctx).authorization.metadata

    tracing_metadata = {
        **(request.model_dump(exclude={"thread_id"})),
        **(metadata.model_dump() if metadata is not None else {}),
    }

    async with request_trace_context(
        name=request.pipeline_type,
        thread_id=request.thread_id,
        metadata=tracing_metadata,
    ):
        try:
            output = await run_pipeline(request)
            return PipelineResponseSuccess(final_output=output)
        except PipelineStepError as e:
            logger.exception(f"Pipeline step failed: {e.step_name}")
            return PipelineResponseFailure(step_name=e.step_name, error=str(e.cause))


async def run_pipeline(request: PipelineRequest) -> BaseModel:
    """Dispatch to the appropriate pipeline's execute() based on request type."""
    match request:
        case QueryBuilderPipelineRequest():
            ctx = QueryBuilderPipelineCtx(
                workspace_ids=request.workspace_ids,
                user_query=request.user_query,
                gremlin_fallback_enabled=request.gremlin_fallback_enabled,
            )
            return await query_builder_pipeline.execute(ctx, ctx)

        case InsightsPipelineRequest():
            insights_ctx = InsightsPipelineCtx(
                report_id=request.report_id,
            )
            return await insights_pipeline.execute(insights_ctx, insights_ctx)

        case _ as unreachable:
            assert_never(unreachable)

import loguru
from ardoq_ai.api.generated.models import GremlinExecutionResponse
from ardoq_ai.api.graph_search.api import search_graph
from ardoq_ai.domain.rag.context import Context, RAGChunk
from ardoq_ai.tools.ardoq_tool.error_handling.exceptions.request_exceptions import (
    BadRequestException,
    ForbiddenRequestException,
    MalformedInputException,
    UnauthorizedException,
    UnexpectedAPIException,
)

from ardoq_ai_eval.config.litellm_context import get_eval_logger
from ardoq_ai_eval.domain.record import SingleTurnRecord
from ardoq_ai_eval.metrics.schemas import MetricEvalResult, SingleTurnMetricName
from ardoq_ai_eval.metrics.single_turn.definitions.gremlin_correctness import gremlin_correctness
from ardoq_ai_eval.metrics.utils import evaluate_general_metric


async def evaluate_gremlin_correctness(record: SingleTurnRecord) -> MetricEvalResult:
    """Execute Gremlin queries and evaluate the results using a custom evaluator.

    Runs both the expected and generated Gremlin queries, builds context
    from the results, and passes everything to the custom evaluator.

    Args:
        record: Record with input (NL query), actual_output (generated query),
            and expected_output (expected query).

    Returns:
        MetricEvalResult with score, reasoning, and pass/fail status.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If expected_output or actual_output is None.
    """
    if record.expected_output is None:
        raise ValueError("Cannot evaluate Gremlin when expected_output is None")
    if record.actual_output is None:
        raise ValueError("Cannot evaluate Gremlin when actual_output is None")

    logger = get_eval_logger()
    expected_result = await _execute_query_safe(record.expected_output, logger)
    generated_result = await _execute_query_safe(record.input, logger)

    created_ctx = _create_query_context(
        nl_query=record.input,
        generated_query=record.actual_output,
        generated_result=generated_result,
        expected_query=record.expected_output,
        expected_result=expected_result,
    )
    ctx_elements = [] if record.context is None else list(record.context.elements)
    ctx_elements.extend(created_ctx.elements)
    updated_context = Context(elements=ctx_elements)
    updated_record = record.model_copy(update={"context": updated_context})

    result = await evaluate_general_metric(updated_record, gremlin_correctness)
    return MetricEvalResult(metric=SingleTurnMetricName.GREMLIN_CORRECTNESS, result=result)


def _create_query_context(
    nl_query: str,
    generated_query: str,
    generated_result: GremlinExecutionResponse,
    expected_query: str,
    expected_result: GremlinExecutionResponse,
) -> Context:
    """Create context with query information for evaluation."""
    chunks = [
        RAGChunk(data={"Natural Language Query": nl_query}),
        RAGChunk(data={"Generated Gremlin Query": generated_query}),
        RAGChunk(data={"Generated Result Count": generated_result.count}),
    ]

    if expected_query:
        chunks.append(RAGChunk(data={"Expected Gremlin Query": expected_query}))

    if expected_result:
        chunks.append(RAGChunk(data={"Expected Result Count": expected_result.count}))
        execution_match = generated_result.count == expected_result.count
        chunks.append(RAGChunk(data={"Execution Match": execution_match}))

    return Context(elements=chunks)


async def _execute_query_safe(query: str, logger: "loguru.Logger") -> GremlinExecutionResponse:
    """Execute a Gremlin query, converting exceptions to error responses."""
    try:
        # base_url/authorization/logger default from the active RequestContext (entered by
        # the ai_observability middleware that drives this eval path).
        return await search_graph(query=query)
    except (
        BadRequestException,
        UnauthorizedException,
        ForbiddenRequestException,
        MalformedInputException,
        UnexpectedAPIException,
    ) as e:
        logger.error(f"Gremlin query execution failed: {e}")
        return GremlinExecutionResponse(
            count=0,
            result=[],
            error=str(e),
        )

(ns ardoq.ai-tools.ontology-api
  {:team "ai"}
  (:require
   [ardoq.ai-tools.ai-tools-service :as ai-tools-service]
   [ardoq.ai-tools.middleware :as middleware]
   [ardoq.ai-tools.ontology :as ontology]
   [ardoq.api.crud-api-v2 :as crud-api]
   [ardoq.api.deliberator :as liberator]
   [ardoq.specs :as specs]
   [clojure.spec.alpha :as s]
   [clojure.string :as str]))

(def ^:private owl-mime->format
  {"text/plain" :dle
   "text/owl-functional" :ofn
   "application/rdf+xml" :owl
   "text/turtle" :ttl})

(def ^:private available-mime-types
  (into ["application/json"] (keys owl-mime->format)))

(s/def ::workspaceIds (s/and ::specs/non-empty-string
                             #(every? (fn [id] (s/valid? ::specs/id id)) (str/split % #","))))
(s/def ::get-ontology-query (s/keys :opt-un [::workspaceIds]))

(defn- owl-format
  "Returns the OWL serialization format keyword for the negotiated media type,
   or nil when deliberator negotiated application/json (the default)."
  [ctx*]
  (owl-mime->format (get-in ctx* [:representation :media-type])))

(defn get-ontology
  "Processes an API request by providing Deliberator with a resource-map that describes the ontology API.
  This API accepts a `?whitespace=` argument in the request to indicate if blank lines should be stripped
  from the response. When `?workspaceIds=` is given, the ontology is scoped to those workspaces' model."
  [{ctx :ctx {{:keys [workspaceIds]} :query} :parameters :as req}]
  (let [workspaceIds (some-> workspaceIds (str/split #",") (->> (map str/trim)))]
    (->> {:allowed? (fn [_] (crud-api/allowed? ai-tools-service/service-config ctx :read))
          :exists? true
          :available-media-types available-mime-types
          :handle-ok (fn [ctx*]
                       (let [fmt (owl-format ctx*)
                             result (->> (ontology/get-ontology! ctx
                                                                 :workspace-ids workspaceIds
                                                                 :format (or fmt :dle))
                                         (middleware/strip-whitespace (:request ctx*)))]
                         (if fmt
                           result
                           {:document result})))}
         (merge crud-api/resource-defaults)
         (liberator/run-resource req))))

(def routes
  [["/ontology" {:get {:name ::get-ontology
                       :summary "Get ontology"
                       :description (str "Returns the OWL ontology for the org, or scoped to one or more "
                                         "workspaces' models when `?workspaceIds=` is given a comma-separated "
                                         "list of workspace IDs. Format is selected via the Accept "
                                         "header: application/json (DLe wrapped in JSON, default), text/plain "
                                         "(DLe), text/owl-functional (OFN), application/rdf+xml (RDF/XML), "
                                         "text/turtle (Turtle).")
                       :parameters {:query ::get-ontology-query}
                       :handler get-ontology}}]])

  "Runs an unsaved report search scoped to specific workspaces, so the Python AI
  backend can route Query Builder queries through ai-tools middleware."
  [{{query-payload :body} :parameters
    ctx :ctx
    {:keys [report-service]} :system :as req}]
  (let [unsaved-report (report-api/coerce query-payload)]
    (->> {:allowed? (fn [_]

(ns ardoq.graphlake.graphlake-api
  (:require
   [ardoq.api.crud-api-v2 :as crud-api]
   [ardoq.api.deliberator :as liberator]
   [ardoq.graphlake.graphlake-service :as graphlake-service]
   [ardoq.router :as router]
   [ardoq.service.feature-service :as feature-service]
   [clojure.spec.alpha :as s]
   [reitit.ring :as ring]))

(defn run-query
  [{{{:keys [language query snapshot branch]} :body} :parameters
    {:keys [graphlake-service]} :system
    ctx :ctx
    :as req}]
  (->> {:post! (fn [_]
                 {::crud-api/result (graphlake-service/run-query! (graphlake-service/->reader-ctx graphlake-service ctx)
                                                                  language
                                                                  query
                                                                  {:snapshot snapshot :branch branch})})}
       (merge crud-api/command-defaults)
       (liberator/run-resource req)))

(defn list-snapshots
  [{{{:keys [branch] :as filters} :query} :parameters
    {:keys [graphlake-service]} :system
    ctx :ctx
    :as req}]
  (->> {:exists? true
        :handle-ok (fn [_]
                     (graphlake-service/list-snapshots! (graphlake-service/->reader-ctx graphlake-service ctx)
                                                        {:branch branch}))}
       (merge crud-api/resource-defaults)
       (liberator/run-resource req)))

(defn list-branches
  [{{:keys [graphlake-service]} :system
    ctx :ctx
    :as req}]
  (->> {:exists? true
        :handle-ok (fn [_]
                     (graphlake-service/list-branches! (graphlake-service/->reader-ctx graphlake-service ctx)))}
       (merge crud-api/resource-defaults)
       (liberator/run-resource req)))

(s/def ::filters map?)
(s/def ::list-snapshot-request
  (s/keys :opt-un [::filters]))

(s/def ::language #{"sparql" "gremlin"})
(s/def ::query string?)
(s/def ::snapshot string?)
(s/def ::branch string?)

(s/def ::query-request
  (s/keys :req-un [::language ::query]
          :opt-un [::snapshot ::branch]))

(def graphlake-api
  (ring/router
   [["/run-query" {:post {:name ::run-query
                          :handler run-query
                          :required-features [::feature-service/core_tmp_graphlake-alpha]
                          :parameters {:body ::query-request}}}]
    ["/list-snapshots" {:get {:name ::list-snapshots
                              :required-features [::feature-service/core_tmp_graphlake-alpha]
                              :handler list-snapshots
                              :parameters {:query ::list-snapshot-request}}}]

    ["/list-branches" {:get {:name ::list-branches
                             :required-features [::feature-service/core_tmp_graphlake-alpha]
                             :handler list-branches}}]]

   (assoc router/default-options :data {:swagger {:tags ["GraphLake API"]}})))

Integration map omitted from analysis.'

Co-dependent applications cannot be enumerated.'

Use get_metamodel to confirm which component types qualify (for example Business Capability, Business Process, Organisational Unit). Identify the Application Owner and any named Subject Matter Expert linked to the subject application via Owns or similar reference. Record both as named accountable parties for the Statement output in Phase 3. If no owner is linked, record: 'OWNERSHIP GAP — No named owner linked to <<comp-name>>.'

        - Review Date

        - DR Plan RPO

        - Recovery Type
        - Manual Workaround
        - DR Test Date
        - DR Test Result
        - Approval Status
        - Last Review Date

        - If DR Plan RPO equals Service RPO: flag 'RPO ZERO MARGIN — Technical recovery point ({DR Plan RPO}h) equals business tolerance ({Service RPO}h). Any degradation in recovery performance breaches business tolerance.'
        - If DR Plan RPO less than Service RPO: record 'RPO — Within tolerance. Margin: {Service RPO minus DR Plan RPO}h.'

        - If DR Test Result is not 'Pass': flag 'GOVERNANCE RISK — Last DR Test Result is '{value}'. Plan has known failure modes.'

        - If Manual Workaround is NOT POPULATED: flag 'READINESS GAP — Manual Workaround not documented. No fallback if automated recovery fails.'
